  "text": "Mara turned. Beyond the stern, the sea was smooth except for a narrow furrow running toward the horizon. The skiff’s rope had gone slack. Whatever it had held was moving away.

Then Daniel began waving both arms.

“The last cross!” he shouted.

Mara snatched the chart from her pocket. Her father’s sixth mark lay inside the harbor, beside the church steps. They had passed it without tying off. The five marks outside the breakwater formed a curve, but the sixth closed it.

Mr. Venn glanced back at the quay. Water rushed through the gap, lifting crates and smashing them against the stone. “We can’t get in.”

Mara looked at the coil of painter around the cleat. “We don’t have to.”

She untied it and fed the line through the skiff’s bow ring. Mr. Venn brought the trawler as close to the breakwater as he dared. Mara stood in the skiff, swinging the free end over her head. Daniel ran down the quay to meet her.

The first throw fell short. On the second, he caught it and dragged it to the iron mooring ring by the church steps. He tied a knot Mara recognized: the one their father had made her practice until she could do it blindfolded.

Far out at sea, the furrow stopped.

The rope beneath the skiff tightened, drawing a dark line through the water between Mara and Daniel. The church bell gave a single, muffled knock. Then the tension vanished, and the skiff drifted gently against the trawler.

Daniel stayed by the ring, one hand on the knot. This time, when Mara waved, he waved back."
